{{short description|Canadian marine mammal researcher}}
'''Kit Kovacs''' is a [[marine mammal]] researcher, best known for her work on biology, conservation and management of [[whales]] and [[Pinniped|seals]]. She is based at the [[Norwegian Polar Institute]] (NPI), [[Tromsø]]<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=http://www.npolar.no/en/people/kit.kovacs/|title=Kit M. Kovacs|website=Norwegian Polar Institute|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref> and is an adjunct professor of biology, marine biology, at the [[University Centre in Svalbard]] (UNIS).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.unis.no/staff/kit-m-kovacs/|title=Kit M. Kovacs|website=unis.no|date=November 24, 2014 |publisher=University Centre in Svalbard|language=en-US|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Kovacs was born in [[Germany (while her father was on military service for Canada)]] and has [[Canadians|Canadian and Norwegian citizenship]]. She received her H.B.Sc. (Biology) in 1979 from [[York University]], [[Toronto]], Canada. In 1982, she was awarded a [[Master of Science]] degree in Biology by the [[Lakehead University]] at [[Thunder Bay]]. Her doctorate (Ph.D) in Zoology was awarded by the [[University of Guelph]] (Guelph) in 1986.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://www.polar-academy.com/CVs/KitKovacs.pdf|title=CV|last=Kovacs|first=Kit|website=polar-academy.com|access-date=June 5, 2016|archive-date=March 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160325175700/http://polar-academy.com/CVs/KitKovacs.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Research career==
Kovacs' teaching career, close to 40 years, started as an assistant professor at the [[University of Waterloo]].<ref name=":0" /> She is now the Svalbard Programme Leader for Norwegian Polar Institute at the [[Norwegian Polar Institute]],<ref name=":1"/> as well as a professor of biology at University Studies on Svalbard (UNIS).<ref name=":2">{{cite web|url=http://store.elsevier.com/Kit-M.-Kovacs/ELS_1005023/|title=Kit M. Kovacs Overview|website=store.elsevier.com|publisher=Elsevier|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.unis.no/staff/kit-m-kovacs|title=Kit M. Kovacs – UNIS|website=UNIS|date=November 24, 2014 |language=en-US|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref>

During her 40-year-long research career,<ref name=":2"/><ref name=":3">{{cite web|url=https://iucn-ccsg.org/people/kit-kovacs|title=Kit Kovacs — Climate Change Specialist Group (CCSG)|website=iucn-ccsg.org|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701001511/https://iucn-ccsg.org/people/kit-kovacs|archive-date=July 1, 2016|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref> Kovacs has studied marine mammal population ecology, biology conservation and management, including satellite tagging of [[Bowhead whale|bowhead whales]] since 2010,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.npolar.no/en/projects/details?pid=2100e794-475f-59d4-b737-1dcf47cebda2|title=Satellite tagging of bowhead whales|website=Norwegian Polar Institute|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref> the [[biopsy]] sampling of whales since 2006,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.npolar.no/en/projects/details?pid=a03720cf-649b-583d-bf43-67cd9afc44f3|title=Biopsy sampling whales|website=Norwegian Polar Institute|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref> and extensive research on seals<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mymultiplesclerosis.co.uk/aww/seal-ripper-sable-island-greenland-shark-zoe-lucas-lisa-natanson/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160608171534/http://mymultiplesclerosis.co.uk/aww/seal-ripper-sable-island-greenland-shark-zoe-lucas-lisa-natanson/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=June 8, 2016|title=Seal Ripper {{!}} Sable Island {{!}} Greenland Shark {{!}} Zoe Lucas {{!}} Lisa Natanson – Animal World Wonders|date=August 9, 2015|website=Animal World Wonders|language=en-US|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref> Kovacs has published over 300 publications, receiving over 18,000 citations, resulting in an [[h-index]] and [[i10-index]] of 69 and 226 respectively.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=D2zo9HUAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao|title=Kit M. Kovacs – Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=February 10, 2020}}</ref><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://vimeo.com/45258327|title=Kit Kovacs – Advice for Students|website=Vimeo|date=July 5, 2012 |access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=Kit Kovacs {{!}} Historical Perspectives Interview Excerpt|date=November 15, 2012|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8CBrJpG6ohs|publisher=Aquatic Mammals Journal|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.unep.org/geo/geo_ice/authors.asp|title=Global Outlook for Ice and Snow|website=www.unep.org|access-date=June 5, 2016|archive-date=June 13, 2007|archive-url=http://webarchive.loc.gov/all/20070613072130/http://www.unep.org/geo/geo_ice/authors.asp|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=FRAMSHORTS|title=ARCTIC ANIMAL FACTS – Hooded seals: the worlds [sic] fastest gainers|date=March 22, 2012|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Od_b4kA9qSU|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref>{{Excessive citations inline|date=January 2021}} Kovacs has also successfully facilitated cooperation between the tourism industry and researchers in the Arctic region.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cnns.no/2015/08/13/successful-cooperation-between-the-tourism-industry-and-researchers/|title=Successful cooperation between the tourism industry and researchers|date=2015|publisher=CNNS|access-date=June 5, 2016|archive-date=August 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160809033326/http://cnns.no/2015/08/13/successful-cooperation-between-the-tourism-industry-and-researchers/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://arcticjournal.com/press-releases/1718/exciting-observations-extraordinary-images|title=Exciting observations – extraordinary images|website=The Arctic Journal|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref>

== Service ==
Kovacs has been the president of the [[Society for Marine Mammalogy]].<ref name=":2" /> She now plays an advisory role as Past President for Life, and is currently serving her third term as the chair of the IUCN's Pinniped Specialist Group.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> She served as a representative to the Standing Scientific Group – Life Science under SCAR from 2012 to 2015,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.forskningsradet.no/servlet/Satellite?blobcol=urldata&blobheader=application%2Fpdf&blobheadername1=Content-Disposition%3A&blobheadervalue1=+attachment%3B+filename%3DMandatfornorskdeltakelseiarbeidsgruppenetilSCAReng.pdf&blobkey=id&blobtable=MungoBlobs&blobwhere=1274505542760&ssbinary=true|title=Mandate for representatives to Standing Scientific Groups and Standing Committees under the Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research (SCAR)|access-date=June 21, 2016|newspaper=Forskningsradet.no|archive-date=August 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160816024222/http://www.forskningsradet.no/servlet/Satellite?blobcol=urldata&blobheader=application%2Fpdf&blobheadername1=Content-Disposition%3A&blobheadervalue1=%20attachment&%20filename=MandatfornorskdeltakelseiarbeidsgruppenetilSCAReng.pdf&blobkey=id&blobtable=MungoBlobs&blobwhere=1274505542760&ssbinary=true|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.forskningsradet.no/prognett-polarforskning/International_Committees/1253966395125|title=International Committees – POLARPROG|author=Written by|publisher=Forskningsradet.no|access-date=June 21, 2016|archive-date=August 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160816025712/http://www.forskningsradet.no/prognett-polarforskning/International_Committees/1253966395125|url-status=dead}}</ref> and as a member of Norway's delegation to the [[Scientific Committee for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://antarcticocean.org/2013/09/aoa-seminar-protecting-antarcticas-ocean-whats-at-stake-for-norway/|title=Antarctic Ocean Alliance|website=antarcticocean.org|access-date=June 5, 2016|archive-date=June 29, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160629192406/http://antarcticocean.org/2013/09/aoa-seminar-protecting-antarcticas-ocean-whats-at-stake-for-norway/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Kovacs has held offices of chairman to the Academic User's Board of the [[Huntsman Marine Science Centre]] (1985–1992), a member of the board of directors for the Huntsman Marine Science Centre (1990–1994), was the secretary of the Canadian National Council for the International Union of Biological Studies (NSERC) from 1989 to 1992, and editorial board bember for the [[Canadian Journal of Zoology]] from 1990 to 1994, a board member for the Arctic Light and Heat (ALV) Programme from Jan 1997– December 31, 2002, at the Norwegian National Research Council, the president of the [[Society for Marine Mammalogy|International Society for Marine Mammalogy]] from 2004 to 2006 and is still a member of its scientific advisory council<ref name=":4">{{cite web|url=https://www.marinemammalscience.org/about-us/committees/|title=Society for Marine Mammalogy|website=Society for Marine Mammalogy|language=en-US|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref> and conservation council,<ref name=":4" /> a member of the Arctic Climate Biodiversity's<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arcticbiodiversity.is |title=Arctic Biodiversity Assessment (ABA) – Home |publisher=Arcticbiodiversity.is |access-date=June 21, 2016}}</ref> Impact Assessment Working Group,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arcticbiodiversity.is/about/authors |title=Arctic Biodiversity Assessment (ABA) – Authors |publisher=Arcticbiodiversity.is |access-date=June 21, 2016}}</ref> as well as a contributing author to the ACIA ([[Arctic Climate Impact Assessment]]) report in Chapter 9: Marine Systems<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.acia.uaf.edu/PDFs/ACIA_Science_Chapters_Final/ACIA_Ch09_Final.pdf |title=Ch9 Final |access-date=June 21, 2016 |archive-date=March 12, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160312073212/http://www.acia.uaf.edu/PDFs/ACIA_Science_Chapters_Final/ACIA_Ch09_Final.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> and Chapter 11: Management and Conservation of Wildlife in a Changing Arctic Environment.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.acia.uaf.edu/PDFs/ACIA_Science_Chapters_Final/ACIA_Ch11_Final.pdf |title=Chapter 11: Management and Conservation of Wildlife in a Changing Arctic Environment |author=David R. Klein |newspaper=Acia.uaf.edu |access-date=June 21, 2016 |archive-date=August 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150824170621/http://www.acia.uaf.edu/PDFs/ACIA_Science_Chapters_Final/ACIA_Ch11_Final.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Kovacs was a committee member in 2003–2006<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.smru.st-andrews.ac.uk/documents/SCOS_03_v7.pdf|title=Scientific Advice on Matters Related to the Management of Seal Populations|date=2003|access-date=June 21, 2016|archive-date=November 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151129183055/http://www.smru.st-andrews.ac.uk/documents/SCOS_03_v7.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.smru.st-andrews.ac.uk/documents/SCOS_04_v7.pdf|title=Scientific Advice on Matters Related to the Management of Seal Populations|date=2004|access-date=June 21, 2016|archive-date=November 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151129183028/http://www.smru.st-andrews.ac.uk/documents/SCOS_04_v7.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.smru.st-andrews.ac.uk/documents/SCOS_05_v2f.pdf|title=Scientific Advice on Matters Related to the Management of Seal Populations|date=2005|access-date=June 21, 2016|archive-date=August 24, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110824032850/http://www.smru.st-andrews.ac.uk/documents/SCOS_05_v2f.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.smru.st-andrews.ac.uk/documents/SCOS_06.pdf|title=Scientific Advice on Matters Related to the Management of Seal Populations|date=2006|access-date=June 21, 2016|archive-date=November 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151129182851/http://www.smru.st-andrews.ac.uk/documents/SCOS_06.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> for the [[Natural Environment Research Council]] (NERC, United Kingdom) Special Committee on Seals (SCOS). Kovacs was an International coordinator for the Ringed Seal Circumpolar Network at the Conservation of Arctic Flora and Fauna (CAFF) from 2000 to 2008,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://brage.bibsys.no/xmlui/bitstream/handle/11250/191472/Rapport143.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y|title=Circumpolar Ringed Seal (Pusa hispida) Monitoring|editor=Kit M. Kovacs|access-date=June 21, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.caff.is/monitoring-series/23-all-monitoring-documents/66-cbmp-coordination-meeting-akureyri-iceland-april-11-12-2002 |title=CAFF – CBMP Coordination Meeting: Akureyri, Iceland: April 11–12, 2002 |publisher=Caff.is |access-date=June 21, 2016}}</ref> a member and leader of the Impacts on Sea Ice Reductions in the NorACIA (Norwegian Arctic Climate Impact Assessment) – Group III, as well as a member of the Barend Sea Advisory Group at NorACIA.<ref name=":0" />

Kovacs is currently on the steering committee for the [[International Union for Conservation of Nature|IUCN]] Species Survival Commission (SSC) Climate Change Specialist Group,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://iucn-ccsg.org/people|title=Participants|website=iucn-ccsg.org|publisher=Climate Change Specialist Group|access-date=June 5, 2016|archive-date=May 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160501025139/https://iucn-ccsg.org/people|url-status=dead}}</ref> a member of the Biodiversity Centre Programme Scientific Committee (Polar Environmental Centre) since 2001,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fallmeeting.agu.org/2015/media-center/press-conferences/|title=AGU Fall Meeting|website=2015 AGU Fall Meeting|language=en-US|access-date=June 5, 2016}}</ref> has been on the Scientific Advisory Board Member for the [[American Cetacean Society]] since 2004,<ref>{{cite journal|editor1-last=Dutton|editor1-first=Ian|title=Climate Change: Challenges to Cetacean Conservation|journal=Journal of the American Cetacean Society|date=2010|volume=39|issue=2}}</ref> serves on the Committee for Scientific Advisers and the Conservation Committee for the [[Society for Marine Mammalogy]],<ref name=":4"/> is a member of the Norwegian Scientific Academy for Polar Research<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.polar-academy.com/pages/Members.htm|title=Members – The Norwegian Scientific Academy for Polar Research|website=www.polar-academy.com|access-date=June 5, 2016|archive-date=May 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160524124226/http://www.polar-academy.com/pages/Members.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> and is on the EU Life Sciences Standing Committee, representing Norway.<ref name=":0" />

Kovacs was also the leader of Marine Mammals Exploring the Oceans Pole to Pole (MEOP) project during the [[International Polar Year]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.forskningsradet.no/en/Newsarticle/International_Polar_Years_unique_research_assistants/1253958608033|title=International Polar Year's unique research assistants|website=www.forskningsradet.no|publisher=The Research Council of Norway|access-date=June 5, 2016|archive-date=August 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160816021808/http://www.forskningsradet.no/en/Newsarticle/International_Polar_Years_unique_research_assistants/1253958608033|url-status=dead}}</ref> and worked on the Barents Sea walrus Ecology project, which focused on studying stock structure, movement patterns and general ecology of Barents Sea walruses in collaboration with Russia (2014–15) and on Pechora walrus abundance, which focused on the abundance determination of Pechora Sea walruses in collaboration with Russia (2011–12).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://iasc.info/images/isira/national-reports/2015/ISIRA_2015_national_report_Germany_Norway.pdf |title=Norway 2015 |newspaper=Iasc.info |access-date= June 21, 2016}}</ref>

* Lakehead University Graduate Entrance Scholarship (1979/80)
* Thunder Bay Field Naturalists' Award (1980/81)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tbfn.net/home|title=Thunder Bay Field Naturalists|newspaper=tbfn.net|access-date=June 21, 2016}}</ref> 
* Ontario Graduate Scholarship (1980–1982)
* AOU Best Student Paper Award (1081/81) 
* Multiple NSERC Postgraduate Science Scholarships (1981/82, 1982/83, 1983/84)
* Commonwealth Scholarship (1982/83)
* University of Guelph Graduate Fellowship (1982/83)
* Norman James Aquatic Mammals Fellowship in 1985<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Kovacs|first1=Kit M.|last2=Lavigne|first2=D. M.|title=Cystophora cristata|journal=American Society of Mammalogists|date=June 16, 1986|volume=258|pages=1–9|url=http://www.science.smith.edu/msi/pdf/i0076-3519-258-01-0001.pdf|archive-date=March 15, 2016|access-date=June 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315175804/http://www.science.smith.edu/msi/pdf/i0076-3519-258-01-0001.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> 
* NSERC/NATO Postdoctoral Fellowship (1986/87)<ref name=":0" />
